encounters.cc: Irritability in newborn following term vaginal delivery

lines: Irritability in newborn following term vaginal delivery
He was delivered at term after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery.
The pregnancy was not regularly monitored, and prenatal records are limited.
Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes were 8 and 9, respectively.
Birth weight was appropriate for gestational age.
Since yesterday, the nursing staff have noticed the infant crying frequently and being difficult to console.
He has had normal feeding but appears restless shortly afterward.
Active Problem List:
- Benign familial macrocephaly
- History of neonatal abstinence syndrome
- History of cow's milk protein-induced proctocolitis (diet-controlled)
Home Medications:
- Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) 400 IU orally daily
Cow's milk protein
- Maternal opioid use disorder
- Paternal benign familial macrocephaly
- Maternal atopic dermatitis
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: None (infant).
No fevers have been recorded, and vital signs are within normal limits.
The baby sneezes and yawns repeatedly during observation.
His skin appears mottled with intermittent goosebumps on his arms and legs.
Clear nasal drainage is present, and he frequently squirms in his bassinet.
Physical examination shows an alert but fussy infant with continuous movements.
There is no cyanosis, cardiac murmur, or respiratory distress.
The remainder of the examination, including abdominal and neurologic assessments, is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Presence of blood in stools for the past week in exclusively breastfed infant

lines: Presence of blood in stools for the past week in exclusively breastfed infant
The patient is a male infant with a history of benign familial macrocephaly and neonatal abstinence syndrome who returns with bloody stools.
The infant is exclusively breastfed, has no history of illness, and was born at term without complications.
His mother reports that the infant seems generally happy, has no fever, and is gaining weight appropriately.
The mother denies any recent changes in her diet except for an increase in dairy consumption.

lines: Parental concern about head size appearing larger than peers at routine check-up
The patient is an infant male with a history of neonatal abstinence syndrome and cow's milk protein-induced proctocolitis who returns for routine pediatric care.
He is brought by his parents for a routine check-up.
The parents express concern that their son's head appears larger than those of other children his age.
They deny any history of developmental delays, seizures, or behavioral changes.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of irritability and projectile vomiting without fever

lines: Two-day history of irritability and projectile vomiting without fever
The 1-year-old male with benign familial macrocephaly, neonatal abstinence syndrome, and diet-controlled cow's milk protein-induced proctocolitis presents with acute symptoms.
The parents report that the infant has been crying more than usual and has had three episodes of projectile vomiting.
There is no history of fever, diarrhea, or cough.
The parents deny any history of trauma or falls.

encounters.cc: Intermittent vomiting with acute loss of head control and decreased responsiveness

lines: Intermittent vomiting with acute loss of head control and decreased responsiveness
The 1-year-old male with benign familial macrocephaly and history of neonatal abstinence syndrome returns for evaluation one month after an emergency department visit for similar symptoms.
The parents report that the vomiting is non-bilious and occurs without any apparent trigger.
They also mention that the infant, who was previously able to sit with support, now seems to have difficulty holding his head up and is less responsive to stimuli.
There is no history of fever, cough, diarrhea, or rash.
